native_mcp_support.notes: Upgraded at the 2026-08-19 refresh from 'framework-level only'. MCP is now a documented first-class feature of the vendor's hosted API as well as its agent stack. Hosted (tier 1, Model Studio): 'Add MCP server information in the tools parameter when using the Responses API', 'Available through the Responses API only', 'Supports MCP servers using the SSE protocol', 'Maximum 10 MCP servers'; supported models include the Qwen3.7-Max / Qwen3.7-3.5-Plus / Qwen3.6-3.5-Flash tiers, the 'Qwen3.6 open-source series (except qwen3.6-27b)' and the 'Qwen3.5 open-source series' - Qwen3.8 ids are not yet listed. Self-host (tier 1, vendor repos): Qwen-Agent takes an mcpServers block in function_list and auto-starts the servers; Qwen Code loads mcpServers from settings.json over stdio (command/args), HTTP (httpUrl) or SSE (url) with includeTools/excludeTools filtering. In every path MCP tool schemas are converted to OpenAI-shaped function definitions and injected as input tokens - MCP is not an in-model protocol.

skills_concept.value: Qwen-Agent tools/plugins + Qwen Code MCP servers (no packaged skill format)
skills_concept.notes: There is no Anthropic-Agent-Skills-style packaged, progressively-disclosed skill bundle. Qwen-Agent ('pip install -U "qwen-agent[gui,rag,code_interpreter,mcp]"') exposes a function_list of tools, plugins, built-ins and mcpServers configs; Qwen Code exposes MCP servers from settings.json. Everything registered is injected in full at request time and billed as input tokens on every turn - there is no lazy loading tier.

release_date.notes: The model card citation gives only month = August, year = 2026 (tier 1). Day precision comes from vLLM's day-0 support announcement for Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B, published 2026-08-12. Conflict noted: OpenRouter shows a 2026-08-03 creation date for the hosted qwen3.8-max endpoint - that is the priced API launch; the open weights landed later, which is what this entry covers.

knowledge_cutoff.notes: The Qwen team publishes no knowledge-cutoff date for the Qwen3.8 series; the model card does not state one. Left null rather than guessed.

context_window_tokens.notes: Model card, Model Overview: 'Context Length: 262,144 natively and extensible up to 1,010,000 tokens.' Confirmed by config.json max_position_embeddings = 262144 and tokenizer_config.json model_max_length = 262144. Shared input+output pool.

input_output_shared.notes: Single causal-LM position budget (max_position_embeddings 262144); prompt, tool definitions, the <think> reasoning trace and the answer all draw on the same pool.

max_input_tokens.notes: Derived: native window 262,144 minus the card's recommended 131,072-token final-response allocation. No vendor max-input cap is published for the open weights - on a self-hosted server the operator sets it with --max-model-len. Note the card's allocation guidance ('Reasoning Content: 262,144; Final Response: 131,072') is written for the 1M extended configuration, so at native 262,144 the reasoning trace and the prompt compete directly.

max_output_tokens_default.notes: The card publishes no per-query default output length for Qwen3.8 (unlike Qwen3.5/3.6, which recommend 32,768). It instead gives a budget allocation, and vLLM's launch post advises setting max_tokens=128,000 for agentic workflows. Defaults are set by the serving stack.

max_output_tokens_max.notes: Card, Best Practices: 'For frameworks that support separate token limits for internal reasoning and final outputs, we suggest the following configuration within the 1M context length: Reasoning Content: Set the maximum output length to 262,144 tokens. Final Response: Set the maximum output length to 131,072 tokens.' 131,072 is the final-response cap; the reasoning trace may consume up to a further 262,144 tokens on top of it.

extended_context.notes: Card: 'extensible up to 1,010,000 tokens' via YaRN RoPE scaling (rope_type yarn, factor 4.0, original_max_position_embeddings 262144), enabled with VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1 / SGLANG_ALLOW_OVERWRITE_LONGER_CONTEXT_LEN=1 plus --max-model-len 1000000. config.json ships rope_type 'default', so the extension is an explicit operator override, not the shipped state. Conflict noted: OpenRouter lists the hosted qwen3.8-max endpoint at 1,000,000 - tier 1 preferred here.

reasoning_tokens_count_as_output.notes: Thinking mode is mandatory for this model - the chat template always emits a <think>...</think> block before the answer and exposes reasoning_effort levels 'xhigh' (default), 'medium' and 'low'. Reasoning tokens are generated tokens: they occupy the output budget and, on a hosted endpoint, bill at the output rate.

tokenizer_family.notes: CORRECTED at the 2026-08-19 refresh. The previous entry said '~151,643 tokens' - that figure comes from the Qwen1-era tokenization note (github.com/QwenLM/Qwen), which describes Qwen-7B ('151,643 regular tokens and 208 control tokens'), a different and much smaller vocabulary. The Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8 generation ships a new tokenizer: config.json reports vocab_size 248320, tokenizer_config.json reports tokenizer_class Qwen2Tokenizer with 33 added special tokens at ids 248,044-248,076 (<|endoftext|>, <|im_start|>/<|im_end|>, vision/video/audio pads, <think>/</think>). The model cards state 'Token Embedding: 248,320 (Padded)'. Still tiktoken-style byte-level BPE.

tokenizer_public.notes: tokenizer.json / tokenizer_config.json are published in the public HuggingFace repo under the model's license; counts are locally reproducible.

tokenizer_access.notes: tokenizer_config.json: tokenizer_class = Qwen2Tokenizer, model_max_length = 262144. Loadable with transformers AutoTokenizer; the chat template (which is what actually renders tool definitions into the prompt) ships in the same file, so apply_chat_template(tools=...) is the accurate way to count an MCP tool surface.

count_tokens_method.value: from transformers import AutoTokenizer; tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('Qwen/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B'); len(tok.apply_chat_template(messages, tools=tools, tokenize=True))
count_tokens_method.notes: Use apply_chat_template with the tools argument rather than encoding the raw JSON: the template wraps tool definitions in a <tools> block plus format instructions, so raw-JSON counts understate the real footprint.

image_token_rule.value: Not applicable - this checkpoint is text-only
image_token_rule.notes: config.json model_type is 'qwen3_5_moe_text' with no vision/text sub-config, and the card states the model 'cannot process multimodal inputs'; multimodal Qwen3.8-Max is offered only through the official hosted API.

audio_token_rule.notes: This checkpoint is text-only ('cannot process multimodal inputs'; config.json model_type qwen3_5_moe_text with no vision sub-config), so no audio rule applies. The shared 248,320-token vocabulary still reserves audio special-token ids, which is a property of the generation's vocabulary, not of this checkpoint.

chars_per_token_estimate.notes: Set to null at the 2026-08-19 refresh. The previous value (3.5) was attributed to the Qwen1 tokenization note, which documents a 151,643-token vocabulary - a different tokenizer from the 248,320-vocab one this generation ships, so the ratio does not carry over. No vendor-published characters-per-token figure exists for the Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8 tokenizer; measure with the published AutoTokenizer instead of estimating.

native_mcp.notes: RE-SOURCED and DOWNGRADED to medium at the 2026-08-19 remediation; the previous citation was the hosted Model Studio MCP page, which lists no Qwen3.8 id. MCP is a serving-stack / agent-framework property for open weights, not an in-model protocol and not a hosted-platform one. Tier-1 vendor path, verbatim from the Qwen-Agent MCP guide: MCP servers are configured as an `mcpServers` dictionary passed in `function_list` ('Pass the MCP configuration when initializing your agent'), e.g. "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "./workspace"]; the guide publishes no server or tool cap and only advises 'Avoid defining unnecessary services to reduce overhead'. Qwen Code, the vendor CLI, loads mcpServers from settings.json over stdio/HTTP/SSE. Medium confidence because the Qwen-Agent guide's worked example is configured for 'qwen3-max' and neither it nor the Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B card names a Qwen3.8 id; what makes the path work is this model's chat template, which carries the <tools>/<tool_call> contract MCP definitions are rendered into. The hosted Model Studio Responses-API MCP route is NOT available for this id as of 2026-08-19.

parallel_tool_calls.notes: RE-SOURCED and DOWNGRADED to medium at the 2026-08-19 remediation. The previous citation was the Model Studio function-calling page's `parallel_tool_calls` parameter, but that page lists no Qwen3.8 id. Per-model evidence: this model's chat_template iterates an assistant message's tool_calls array ('{%- for tool_call in message.tool_calls %}'), so more than one call per assistant turn is representable in the wire format the weights were trained on. Medium rather than high because neither the model card nor any Qwen3.8-specific vendor page states parallel tool calling as a supported feature or exposes a `parallel_tool_calls` switch for this id.

max_tools_hard.notes: NULL, and DOWNGRADED from high to medium at the 2026-08-19 remediation. No tier-1 page states a per-request numeric cap on the number of tools for this id. Searched: the Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B model card and README (no tool-calling section at all), its tokenizer_config.json chat template (renders a <tools> block with no count rule), its vLLM recipe, and the Model Studio function-calling reference - which describes the OpenAI-style `tools` array without a maximum but lists no Qwen3.8 id. Scope note: the limits that DO bind are (1) the empirical ~30-50-tool selection cliff (see max_tools_practical) and (2) the 262,144-token context window shared by tool definitions, prompt, the mandatory reasoning trace and the answer. The hosted 'Maximum 10 MCP servers' Responses-API cap does not cover this id. There is no documented per-MCP-server tool cap.

max_tools_practical.notes: Empirical, not spec. No Qwen-specific published degradation point exists. Anchors: 'Scaling Enterprise Agent Routing' (arXiv 2606.17519, 2026-06-16) measured routing F1 dropping 16-23 percentage points across three frontier models as a catalog scaled from 10 agents to 110 agents / 584 tools; MCP-Atlas (arXiv 2602.00933) exposes only 10-25 tools per task by design. 40 is a conservative mid-point of the community ~30-50 range for a capable model. Aggregate scope (all connected servers + built-ins combined).

tool_definition_shape.notes: RE-SOURCED 2026-08-19. Tools are supplied as OpenAI-shaped {"type":"function","function":{"name","description","parameters"}} JSON over the OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions endpoint that vLLM/SGLang expose, and this model's own chat_template converts them into the on-the-wire prompt shape: a <tools> block plus 'Function calls MUST follow the specified format: an inner <function=...></function> block must be nested within <tool_call></tool_call>'. The model's vLLM recipe serves it with '--enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder', which is the parser that turns that XML back into OpenAI-shaped tool_calls. Note the shape difference matters for footprint: the rendered XML is not the same token count as the raw function JSON.

tool_defs_count_as_input.notes:
RE-SOURCED 2026-08-19 to this model's own chat template. tokenizer_config.json renders the `tools` argument into a system-message block - '# Tools

You have access to the following functions:

<tools>' - so tool JSON is serialized into the prompt and consumes input context on every request. Corroboration (weaker, coverage caveat): the Model Studio context-cache reference states 'for function calling, if a request includes the `tools` parameter, the tool definition is included in the system message for cache calculation' and 'tool definitions cannot be cached independently', but that page lists no Qwen3.8 id.

tool_search_deferral.notes: No runtime tool-search / deferred-definition-loading mechanism (the Claude ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH / defer_loading equivalent) is documented for Qwen. The nearest facility is static filtering in Qwen Code - per-server includeTools/excludeTools allow/deny lists and global mcp.allowed / mcp.excluded globs - which shrinks the catalog before the request, not lazily during it. Qwen Code does discover servers progressively: 'sending a prompt before MCP finishes simply means the model sees the tools that are ready at that moment'.

max_tool_name_len.notes: No character-count or character-class cap on tool names is published. Model Studio only recommends: 'The name field is a custom tool function name. We recommend using the same name as the function, such as get_current_weather or get_current_time.' Long client-namespaced MCP names therefore cost tokens rather than being rejected. Coverage caveat added 2026-08-19: the cited Model Studio page's supported-model list contains no Qwen3.8 entry of any kind (its newest open-source entries are the Qwen3.6 and Qwen3.5 series), so this records the vendor's documented Qwen tool-calling contract generally rather than a statement about this id.

tools_mcp.tool_schema_limits_notes: No documented JSON-Schema depth, property-count or keyword restrictions for Qwen tool definitions. The Model Studio function-calling reference only recommends that the `name` field match the implementing function (e.g. get_current_weather); no length or character-class rule is published. The practical constraint is the input token budget. The chat template renders tools into a <tools> block and requires calls inside <tool_call></tool_call> tags. For this model the template additionally requires an inner <function=...></function> block nested inside <tool_call></tool_call>, and vLLM/SGLang need --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder to parse it.

max_tool_description_len.notes: No vendor cap on description length; the description is serialized into the <tools> block and counts against the shared 262,144-token window. Coverage caveat added 2026-08-19: the cited Model Studio page's supported-model list contains no Qwen3.8 entry of any kind (its newest open-source entries are the Qwen3.6 and Qwen3.5 series), so this records the vendor's documented Qwen tool-calling contract generally rather than a statement about this id.

max_request_size.notes: No maximum request body size in bytes/MB is documented. The Model Studio rate-limit reference governs throughput instead (600 RPM and 1,000,000-5,000,000 TPM per open-source model id); for self-hosting the bound is the serving config (--max-model-len / --max-num-batched-tokens) and GPU memory. Coverage caveat added 2026-08-19: the cited Model Studio page's supported-model list contains no Qwen3.8 entry of any kind (its newest open-source entries are the Qwen3.6 and Qwen3.5 series), so this records the vendor's documented Qwen tool-calling contract generally rather than a statement about this id.

max_tool_result_size.notes: No documented ceiling on a single tool result. A result is ordinary conversation content, so it is bounded by the 262,144-token window (or --max-model-len on a self-hosted server) shared with the tool definitions and the reasoning trace.

max_parallel_tool_calls_count.notes: `parallel_tool_calls` is a boolean switch; no numeric ceiling on how many calls may be emitted in one turn is published. The practical bound is the remaining output budget. Coverage caveat added 2026-08-19: the cited Model Studio page's supported-model list contains no Qwen3.8 entry of any kind (its newest open-source entries are the Qwen3.6 and Qwen3.5 series), so this records the vendor's documented Qwen tool-calling contract generally rather than a statement about this id.

tool_use_per_turn_limit.notes: No model-level cap on tool-call/result cycles per turn. Qwen Code (the vendor's own CLI host) documents a per-tool-call `timeout` defaulting to 10 minutes and a `discoveryTimeoutMs` handshake timeout (30s stdio / 5s remote) but no cycle cap; agentic loops are bounded by the host and by context.

max_connected_servers.notes: NULLED at the 2026-08-19 remediation (previously 10 at high confidence). The Model Studio MCP reference does state 'Maximum 10 MCP servers.', but it is a hosted Responses-API platform cap, and that page's supported-model list reads "Qwen-Max: Qwen3.7-Max series; Qwen-Plus: Qwen3.7-Plus series, Qwen3.6-Plus series, Qwen3.5-Plus series; Qwen-Flash: Qwen3.6-Flash series, Qwen3.5-Flash series; Qwen3.6 open-source series (except qwen3.6-27b); Qwen3.5 open-source series" - i.e. there is no Qwen3.8 entry on that list at all, so asserting the cap for this id was unsupported. Searched for a replacement: the Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B model card and README, its tokenizer_config.json chat template, its vLLM recipe and the Qwen-Agent MCP guide all publish no server-count cap. No per-request numeric cap on connected MCP servers is documented for this model; what binds is the 262,144-token window shared by tool definitions, prompt, reasoning and output, the empirical ~30-50-tool selection cliff, and the agent host.

max_total_tools.notes: RE-SOURCED 2026-08-19 from a vLLM recipe page named for Qwen3.5 to this model's own vLLM recipe. Tier 4: a serving-framework doc, not a vendor spec. It documents '--max-model-len 262144' (extensible to 1M) with '--enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder' and documents no numeric ceiling on the number of tools. No aggregate tool-count cap is published at the model layer; the effective aggregate ceiling is derived - (262,144 - reasoning and answer headroom) / average tool-definition tokens - and is set by the operator's --max-model-len. Host layers cap lower in practice (Cursor ~40 tools, Claude Desktop ~100). The hosted Responses-API 10-server cap does not cover this id.

tools_mcp.other_limits_notes: Open-weight: the model API layer publishes no tool count/size cap, and - CORRECTED 2026-08-19 - no Qwen3.8 id appears on the hosted Model Studio MCP, function-calling, context-cache, batch or pricing pages, so none of the Model Studio platform caps (including 'Maximum 10 MCP servers' on the Responses API) can be asserted for this model. Binding limits, in the order they usually bite: (1) the 262,144-token context window shared by tool definitions + prompt + reasoning + output, with the mandatory <think> trace competing directly for it; (2) the empirical ~30-50-tool selection cliff; (3) the serving stack - vLLM/SGLang --max-model-len, --max-num-batched-tokens and KV cache, plus a matching --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder and --reasoning-parser qwen3 (without the tool parser the model's <tool_call> XML is returned as plain text); (4) the agent host - Qwen-Agent mcpServers configs and Qwen Code includeTools/excludeTools and mcp.allowed/mcp.excluded filters with a 10-minute default tool-call timeout, and third-party hosts cap lower (Cursor ~40 tools, Claude Desktop ~100).

strict_function_schema.notes: No OpenAI-style `strict` structured-function mode (100-property / 5-level / no-oneOf enforcement) is documented for Qwen. Schemas are passed through as ordinary JSON Schema. Coverage caveat added 2026-08-19: the cited Model Studio page's supported-model list contains no Qwen3.8 entry of any kind (its newest open-source entries are the Qwen3.6 and Qwen3.5 series), so this records the vendor's documented Qwen tool-calling contract generally rather than a statement about this id.

skills_supported.notes: No packaged, model-invokable 'skill' format analogous to Anthropic Agent Skills. The vendor's agent stack is Qwen-Agent (pip install -U "qwen-agent[gui,rag,code_interpreter,mcp]"), which exposes a function_list of tools/plugins and mcpServers configs, and Qwen Code, which loads MCP servers from settings.json. Both are tool wiring, not a progressive-disclosure skill bundle: everything configured is injected up front.

skills_loading_model.notes: No skill system, so no loading model. Tools/plugins registered in Qwen-Agent's function_list or Qwen Code's mcpServers are always-on for the session and injected in full at request time.

skills_context.skills_context_cost_notes: No skills system to cost. The context cost that matters is the tool surface: MCP tool schemas are translated to OpenAI-shaped function definitions, rendered into the chat template's <tools> block, and counted as input tokens on every request in the conversation - they are re-sent each turn, so the footprint is multiplied by turn count unless a prefix cache absorbs it.
skills_context.system_prompt_overhead_notes: System prompt is billed as input tokens. Tool definitions are folded into the system message for cache-prefix purposes (Model Studio context-cache reference), so system prompt + tool JSON form one contiguous prefix. No fixed platform-injected overhead is documented for self-hosted deployments.

prompt_caching.notes: Self-host value. vLLM's Qwen recipe for this generation serves with --enable-prefix-caching, so a stable system prompt + tool-definition prefix is recomputed once and reused - the main lever for a large MCP tool surface on a multi-turn agent loop. Hosted: the Model Studio context-cache reference lists neither qwen3.8 nor any open-source Qwen id, so no hosted cache discount is documented for this model as of 2026-08-19.

memory_feature.notes: No built-in cross-session memory in the model or in the open-source serving path. Qwen-Agent ships RAG/memory helper modules that an application can wire up, but they are application state injected as ordinary input tokens, not a model feature.

input_per_mtok_usd.notes: No tier-1 price. The Alibaba Cloud Model Studio pricing page carries no qwen3.8 row at all as of 2026-08-19 (its newest entries are qwen3.7-max/plus, qwen3.6-*, qwen3.5-*), and the open-source pricing table has no qwen3.8 id. Tier-3 for reference only: OpenRouter lists the hosted qwen3.8-max endpoint at $2/M input and $6/M output - a different product from these open weights. Self-hosted, cost is compute.

output_per_mtok_usd.notes: Same as input: no tier-1 qwen3.8 row on the Model Studio pricing page. OpenRouter (tier 3) shows $6/M output for the hosted qwen3.8-max endpoint. Remember the reasoning trace bills as output on any hosted endpoint, and this model always thinks.

cached_input_per_mtok_usd.notes: No cached-input price: the Model Studio context-cache reference (explicit cache = 10% of input price, implicit = 20%) lists no qwen3.8 id and no open-source Qwen id.

batch_discount.notes: Batch inference is documented at '50% of the real-time inference price' for both input and output, but the supported-model list is qwen-max / qwen-plus / qwen-flash / qwen-turbo (Singapore) and the commercial qwen3.7/3.6/3.5 tiers (Beijing). No qwen3.8 id and no open-source Qwen id appears, so no batch discount is documented for this model.

billing_unit.notes: Model Studio bills per input and output token; open weights under the qwen3.8-max license are otherwise a pure compute cost.

cost.multimodal_billing_notes: Not applicable to this checkpoint: it is text-only (config.json model_type qwen3_5_moe_text, and the card states it cannot process multimodal inputs). Multimodal Qwen3.8-Max is available only through the official hosted API, whose rates are not published on the Alibaba Cloud Model Studio pricing page as of 2026-08-19.

reasoning_billed_as_output.notes: Thinking is mandatory - the chat template always produces a <think> block, at reasoning_effort xhigh by default - so the reasoning trace is generated output on every request and is charged at the output rate on any hosted endpoint. With a recommended reasoning allocation of up to 262,144 tokens this dominates cost on agentic runs.

self_host.framework_tool_calling_notes: vLLM/SGLang: add --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder (per vLLM's Qwen3.8 launch post) plus --reasoning-parser qwen3 to split the mandatory <think> block out of the answer; without the tool-call parser the model's <tool_call> XML is returned as plain text and the client sees no tool call. vLLM's post advises budgeting max_tokens=128_000 for agentic workflows. Qwen-Agent supplies the MCP layer (mcpServers in function_list); Qwen Code loads MCP servers from settings.json over stdio/HTTP/SSE. Because thinking cannot be disabled, every agent turn pays reasoning tokens on top of the tool-definition prefix.

models.notes: Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B is the open-weight release of Qwen3.8-Max, the flagship of the Qwen3.8 generation (August 2026) and the largest open-weight Qwen to date at 2.4T total / 95B activated parameters. It is text-only, thinking-always-on with three reasoning_effort levels (xhigh default / medium / low), and ships under a custom source-available 'qwen3.8-max' licence rather than Apache-2.0. Card benchmarks emphasise agentic work: Terminal Bench 2.1 86.6, SWE-bench Pro 67.7, DeepSWE 1.1 56.6, CoWorkBench 74.8. For MCP work the practical caveats are the mandatory reasoning budget (recommended up to 262,144 tokens) competing with tool definitions inside the 262,144-token native window, and the absence of any hosted Model Studio listing (so no documented context cache, batch discount or tier-1 price).

release_date.notes: Tier-1 gives month only: the model card citation reads month = August, year = 2026. Day precision is tier-4 - a release tracker reports 'Alibaba shipped the open weights for Qwen3.8-27B on the evening of August 14, 2026, landing the repository on Hugging Face and ModelScope'. Consistent with the HuggingFace org listing, which showed the repo 'Updated 3-4 days ago' when checked on 2026-08-19. Treat the day as approximate.

No vendor max-input cap is published; on a self-hosted server the operator sets it via --max-model-len. The card's allocation advice is framed 'within the 1M context length', so at the native 262,144 window the reasoning trace competes directly with the prompt.

max_output_tokens_default.notes: Qwen3.8 drops the per-query default that Qwen3.5/3.6 carried ('an output length of 32,768 tokens for most queries'); the card publishes only a maximum allocation. Defaults are set by the serving stack.

max_output_tokens_max.notes: Card, Best Practices - Adequate Output Length: 'For frameworks that support separate token limits for internal reasoning and final outputs, we suggest the following configuration within the 1M context length: Reasoning Content: Set the maximum output length to 262,144 tokens. native_mcp.notes: RE-SOURCED at the 2026-08-19 remediation. The previous citation was the hosted Model Studio MCP reference, which EXPLICITLY EXCLUDES this id. The Model Studio MCP reference's supported-model list reads "Qwen-Max: Qwen3.7-Max series; Qwen-Plus: Qwen3.7-Plus series, Qwen3.6-Plus series, Qwen3.5-Plus series; Qwen-Flash: Qwen3.6-Flash series, Qwen3.5-Flash series; Qwen3.6 open-source series (except qwen3.6-27b); Qwen3.5 open-source series". For open weights MCP support is a serving-stack / agent-framework property, not a hosted-platform one, and this model's own tier-1 HuggingFace card carries it: the Agentic Usage section says 'We recommend using Qwen-Agent to quickly build Agent applications with Qwen3.6' and ships an MCP example verbatim - tools = [{'mcpServers': {"filesystem": {"command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "/Users/xxxx/Desktop"]}}}] - alongside 'Qwen Code is an open-source AI agent for the terminal, optimized for Qwen models' and the --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder serving flag. parallel_tool_calls.notes: Tier-1: Model Studio documents a `parallel_tool_calls` request parameter - 'set the parallel_tool_calls request parameter to true' - so all tool calls are returned simultaneously. The Qwen function-calling guide adds that 'the current default tool calling template natively supports Parallel Function Calls'.

max_tools_hard.notes: No per-request numeric cap on the number of tools is documented for Qwen at the model-API layer: the Model Studio function-calling reference lists the 'Qwen3.6 open source' series among the models that support function calling and describes the OpenAI-style `tools` array without stating a maximum, and self-hosted vLLM/SGLang enforce no tool count. Scope note, CORRECTED 2026-08-19: the hosted 'Maximum 10 MCP servers' Responses-API cap is out of scope for this id (that page's supported-model list reads "Qwen-Max: Qwen3.7-Max series; Qwen-Plus: Qwen3.7-Plus series, Qwen3.6-Plus series, Qwen3.5-Plus series; Qwen-Flash: Qwen3.6-Flash series, Qwen3.5-Flash series; Qwen3.6 open-source series (except qwen3.6-27b); Qwen3.5 open-source series".). The limits that DO bind here are (1) the empirical ~30-50-tool selection cliff (see max_tools_practical) and (2) the 262,144-token context window shared by tool definitions, prompt and output, i.e. window / average tool-definition tokens. There is no documented per-MCP-server tool cap.

max_tools_practical.notes: Empirical, not spec. No Qwen-specific published degradation point exists. Anchors: 'Scaling Enterprise Agent Routing' (arXiv 2606.17519, 2026-06-16) measured routing F1 dropping 16-23 percentage points across three frontier models as a catalog scaled from 10 agents to 110 agents / 584 tools; MCP-Atlas (arXiv 2602.00933) exposes only 10-25 tools per task by design. 40 is a conservative mid-point of the community ~30-50 range for a capable model. Aggregate scope (all connected servers + built-ins combined).

tool_definition_shape.notes: Tier-1: tools are supplied as {"type":"function","function":{"name","description","parameters"}} with JSON-Schema parameters, over the OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions endpoint that both Model Studio and self-hosted vLLM/SGLang expose. The Qwen function-calling guide notes the chat template 'has already included support for the Hermes-style tool use'; vLLM ships both `hermes` and `qwen3_coder` parsers, and the Qwen recipes use --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder for this generation.

tool_defs_count_as_input.notes: Tier-1 confirmation: the Model Studio context-cache reference states that 'for function calling, if a request includes the `tools` parameter, the tool definition is included in the system message for cache calculation' and that 'tool definitions cannot be cached independently'. Tool JSON is therefore serialized into the prompt and billed as input tokens; on a self-hosted deployment it is rendered into the chat template and consumes context.

tool_search_deferral.notes: No runtime tool-search / deferred-definition-loading mechanism (the Claude ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH / defer_loading equivalent) is documented for Qwen. The nearest facility is static filtering in Qwen Code - per-server includeTools/excludeTools allow/deny lists and global mcp.allowed / mcp.excluded globs - which shrinks the catalog before the request, not lazily during it. Qwen Code does discover servers progressively: 'sending a prompt before MCP finishes simply means the model sees the tools that are ready at that moment'.

max_tool_name_len.notes: No character-count or character-class cap on tool names is published. Model Studio only recommends: 'The name field is a custom tool function name. We recommend using the same name as the function, such as get_current_weather or get_current_time.' Long client-namespaced MCP names therefore cost tokens rather than being rejected.

tools_mcp.tool_schema_limits_notes: No documented JSON-Schema depth, property-count or keyword restrictions for Qwen tool definitions. The Model Studio function-calling reference only recommends that the `name` field match the implementing function (e.g. get_current_weather); no length or character-class rule is published. The practical constraint is the input token budget. The chat template renders tools into a <tools> block and requires calls inside <tool_call></tool_call> tags. vLLM/SGLang for this generation need --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder plus --reasoning-parser qwen3. The model card reports MCPMark 37.0 for the sibling 35B-A3B, measured against GitHub MCP with a standard tool schema, indicating standard MCP schemas are handled without special shaping.

max_tool_description_len.notes: No vendor cap on description length; the description is serialized into the <tools> block and counts against the shared 262,144-token window.

max_request_size.notes: No maximum request body size in bytes/MB is documented. The Model Studio rate-limit reference governs throughput instead (600 RPM and 1,000,000-5,000,000 TPM per open-source model id); for self-hosting the bound is the serving config (--max-model-len / --max-num-batched-tokens) and GPU memory.

max_tool_result_size.notes: No documented ceiling on a single tool result. A result is ordinary conversation content, so it is bounded by the 262,144-token window (or --max-model-len on a self-hosted server) shared with the tool definitions and the reasoning trace.

max_parallel_tool_calls_count.notes: `parallel_tool_calls` is a boolean switch; no numeric ceiling on how many calls may be emitted in one turn is published. The practical bound is the remaining output budget.

tool_use_per_turn_limit.notes: No model-level cap on tool-call/result cycles per turn. strict_function_schema.notes: No OpenAI-style `strict` structured-function mode (100-property / 5-level / no-oneOf enforcement) is documented for Qwen. Schemas are passed through as ordinary JSON Schema.

skills_supported.notes: No packaged, model-invokable 'skill' format analogous to Anthropic Agent Skills. skills_loading_model.notes: No skill system, so no loading model. Tools/plugins registered in Qwen-Agent's function_list or Qwen Code's mcpServers are always-on for the session and injected in full at request time.

skills_context.skills_context_cost_notes: No skills system to cost. The context cost that matters is the tool surface: MCP tool schemas are translated to OpenAI-shaped function definitions, rendered into the chat template's <tools> block, and counted as input tokens on every request in the conversation - they are re-sent each turn, so the footprint is multiplied by turn count unless a prefix cache absorbs it.
skills_context.system_prompt_overhead_notes: System prompt is billed as input tokens. Tool definitions are folded into the system message for cache-prefix purposes (Model Studio context-cache reference), so system prompt + tool JSON form one contiguous prefix. No fixed platform-injected overhead is documented for self-hosted deployments.

prompt_caching.notes: Scope split, corrected at the 2026-08-19 refresh. memory_feature.notes: No built-in cross-session memory in the model or in the open-source serving path. Qwen-Agent ships RAG/memory helper modules that an application can wire up, but they are application state injected as ordinary input tokens, not a model feature.

tokenizer_family.notes: CORRECTED at the 2026-08-19 refresh. The previous entry said '~151,643 tokens' - that figure comes from the Qwen1-era tokenization note (github.com/QwenLM/Qwen), which describes Qwen-7B ('151,643 regular tokens and 208 control tokens'), a different and much smaller vocabulary. tokenizer_public.notes: tokenizer.json / tokenizer_config.json are published in the public HuggingFace repo under the model's license; counts are locally reproducible.

tokenizer_access.notes: tokenizer_config.json: tokenizer_class = Qwen2Tokenizer, model_max_length = 262144. count_tokens_method.value: from transformers import AutoTokenizer; tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B'); len(tok.apply_chat_template(messages, tools=tools, tokenize=True))
count_tokens_method.notes: Use apply_chat_template with the tools argument rather than encoding the raw JSON: the template wraps tool definitions in a <tools> block plus format instructions, so raw-JSON counts understate the real footprint.

image_token_rule.value: Variable: the vision encoder patches an image into a resolution-dependent number of visual tokens; no closed-form per-image formula is published
image_token_rule.notes: Alibaba's vision reference states only that 'the total token count for all images and text must not exceed the model's maximum input' and that the number of images per request is 'determined by the model's total token limit' - it publishes no pixels-per-token constant or per-image cap. The model card gives no formula either. Count multimodal input with the model's AutoProcessor rather than estimating.

audio_token_rule.notes: The model card scopes this model to text, image and video input; audio is handled by the separate Qwen3-Omni / Qwen3.5-Omni line. serving_frameworks.notes: vLLM ships a maintained Qwen3.5 recipe with text-only (--language-model-only), multimodal-with-tool-calling and latency-optimised variants, all using --reasoning-parser qwen3 and --enable-prefix-caching.

self_host.framework_tool_calling_notes: vLLM's Qwen3.5 recipe gives the canonical tool-calling command: '--reasoning-parser qwen3 --enable-prefix-caching --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder'. Prefix caching matters here: the tool-definition block sits at the head of every request, so caching it is what keeps a multi-turn MCP session affordable. MCP arrives via Qwen-Agent, Qwen Code, or Alibaba's hosted Responses API (the 'Qwen3.5 open-source series' is on its supported list; max 10 MCP servers, SSE only).

models.notes: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B is the sparse member of the Qwen3.5 generation, open-sourced 2026-02-16 - the generation that introduced this tokenizer (248,320 vocab) and the 262,144-token native window that Qwen3.6 and Qwen3.8 inherit. TWO GENERATIONS SUPERSEDED (by Qwen3.6, April 2026, and Qwen3.8, August 2026) but still GA: Apache-2.0 weights remain published, the id is still priced on Alibaba's Model Studio open-source table ($0.25/$2.0 per M - the cheapest entry in this file), and it does not appear on Model Studio's decommissioning list (which does schedule a large batch of Qwen3-era ids for retirement on 2026-10-10). Retained here as the cheap, small-footprint baseline for MCP hosting comparisons.
